transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (CTO, Nebula), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Ellen Kim (PM)
Meeting type: POC scoping — cost model + benchmarks

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and unit economics. Customer is interested in comparing Dedicated vs Hosted run for their autonomous fleet telemetry summarization pipeline; primary constraints are latency SLOs (p95 <= 350ms), and an ops budget of ~$12k/month.

Topics covered:
- Workload characterization (avg tokens, seq length, qps)
- Per-token cost modeling and batching/caching knobs
- Benchmark plan and timeline for a 4-week POC
- Security/compliance check for Private option
- Next steps and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Samira from Redwood, with Liam our solutions engineer, we just wanted to run through the poc scope for Nebula Robotics - cost modeling and the benchmark plan, ok?
[00:12] Marco: yep thanks Samira, appreciate it. quick context first, we process telemetry and natural language summaries for fleet ops — so requests vary a lot, some are short commands 40-60 tokens, others are 2k token summaries, average today about 600 tokens per request.
[00:26] Priya: yeah and throughput peaks at around 18 rps during batch offload windows, steady 4-6 rps otherwise, latency is important because crews need near-realtime feedback.
[00:37] Liam: great that helps. rough numbers help us pick the right model config and batching strategy. if avg is ~600 tokens and p95 target 350ms, Dedicated GPU with optimized kernels or a trimmed lower-latency model make sense.
[00:50] Ellen: can you clarify cost per token estimates please, how do you compute that?
[00:54] Samira: sure — we break it into unit compute cost + infra overhead + plus small slice for management. for hosted endpoints our ballpark for mid-sized open models is $0.00045 per token served at default settings; Dedicated reduces effective per-token by approx 30% depending on utilization and batching; additional savings from KV/prefix caching if requests reuse context — that can cut token volume by another 25-50% for your workload potentially. these are roughs we will nail down with trace data.
[01:23] Marco: ok so Dedicated might get us near $0.0003 per token with heavy batching?
[01:27] Liam: yeah in high utilization steady-state maybe 0.00028-0.00035 range; important caveat — latency SLOs limit how much batching we can do. for p95 350ms we might batch up to ~5-8 requests depending on model latency curves. we'll include batching knobs in the POC.
[01:43] Priya: whats the plan for the benchmark — we want a 72-hour run that mimics peak windows and tail latency.
[01:49] Liam: recommended: 72-hour benchmark on Dedicated reserved pool with two phases: Phase A simulate peak-day traffic (18 rps bursts) for 24 hours, Phase B steady-state 4-6 rps for 48 hours. Collect token counts, latency distributions, GPU utilization, and per-token cost. We'll also run a hosted baseline for comparison.
[02:06] Samira: and we'll include a run where KV cache is enabled with your typical prefix reuse to measure effective token savings. Priya, you mentioned many repeated prompts — that'll show up well in cache experiments.
[02:16] Priya: yes about 40% of requests reuse a common 1200-token prefix from sensor metadata.
[02:22] Marco: on budgeting — our ops budget is approx $12k/month for inference across fleet, we need to know if POC proves out dedicated will fit that or if hosted is cheaper.
[02:31] Liam: rough math here — if you do 1.2M tokens/day (ex: 600 tokens * 2000 requests), that's 36M tokens/month. at hosted $0.00045/token = $16,200/month — over budget. Dedicated with caching & batching could bring that to ~ $9k-$11k/month depending on achieved cache hit and batching. so it's plausible but depends on real telemetry.
[02:53] Ellen: that matches our concern. we need concrete numbers to present to CFO.
[02:58] Samira: understood. POC deliverable will include a baseline cost model + sensitivity analysis (cache hit% x batching factor) so you can see ranges. we'll produce a spreadsheet and run the benchmark to pin the realistic point estimates.
[03:10] Marco: security — we might need Private (VPC) since some telemetry is regulated. do you support on-prem or VPC?
[03:15] Samira: yes Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs. we'll attach SOC2 artifact and the architecture note. disclaimer: the Private deployment adds platform fee which we will show in the pricing sheet.
[03:27] Priya: KMS — is that customer-managed?
[03:30] Liam: yes customer-managed KMS supported, sometimes the ASR in docs shows K-M-S but it's KMS for keys, and we can do BYOK flows.
[03:36] Marco: good. timeline wise what is realistic?
[03:39] Liam: typical POC timeline: week 0-1 align & ingest traces + config, week 2 deploy benchmark harness and smoke runs, week 3 run the 72-hour benchmark and analyze, week 4 present results with recommendations and pricing. overall 4 weeks-ish. if you need Private on-prem install it can add 1-2 weeks to that due to networking/compliance.
[04:02] Ellen: what about evaluation metrics beyond cost? we'll need quality regression checks.
[04:06] Samira: yes we'll include evals vs your golden prompts — quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to the prompt sets. we'll run A/B between model variants to show quality vs cost tradeoff.
[04:16] Priya: for the benchmark config can you recommend model families? we currently use Llama-family internally.
[04:20] Liam: we typically test a compact low-latency variant and a standard higher-quality variant — e.g., Llama2-13B-8k quantized for latency and Llama-70B equivalent (or best open alternative) for quality baseline. we'll include quantized variants and measure token/sec and memory.
[04:34] Marco: references to prior benchmarks?
[04:36] Samira: we'll share our benchmark report and a pricing/workbook template — link: https://redwood-inference.com/docs/poc-pricing (placeholder) and a sample benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:45] Priya: great — for the caching experiments do you emulate partial prefix matches too? some requests have slightly mutated metadata.
[04:50] Liam: yes we test exact and fuzzy prefix reuse, cache TTL and eviction policies are part of the experiment. we'll show effective reduced token delta.
[04:58] Marco: risk: what if we can't meet 350ms p95 with Dedicated due to long seqs?
[05:03] Liam: mitigation: two prong. first: model/quantization choices reduce per-token latency; second: we can route latency-sensitive requests to a lower-capacity low-latency endpoint (Hosted or smaller model) and send heavy batch summarizations to Dedicated. Redwood's smart routing can fallback automatically. we'll simulate mixed routing in the POC.
[05:22] Ellen: who is responsible for instrumentation? we can give traces but do you need an SDK?
[05:26] Samira: minimal — trace CSV with timestamp, tokens per request, and label is enough. Liam will provide a small harness script that replays traces into the Redwood benchmark harness.
[05:34] Priya: ok we'll export last week's traces and scrub PII.
[05:38] Marco: success criteria — what do we accept at end of POC?
[05:41] Samira: good to formalize — proposed: 1) Demonstrate p95 <= 350ms for at least 95% of traffic in a mixed routing config, 2) Effective per-token cost <= your $12k/month ops budget once scaled, 3) No show-stopping security gaps (SOC2 docs reviewed). If those are met we'd move to Reserved Dedicated capacity commitment.
[06:01] Marco: sounds good.
[06:03] Samira: recap of next steps: I'll send pricing workbook; Liam will send benchmark config; Marco will send traces; security team will get SOC2 artifacts. Schedule the benchmark week of 2026-03-16?
[06:15] Priya: that week works, we'll confirm by Friday.
[06:18] Samira: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[06:22] Marco: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
